messages:
acme_ops: Hey team — over the last few hours we've been seeing a bunch of 429s and big latency jumps. App is configured to prefer eu-region, but requests are getting routed to us-west and failing under burst. Example request ids: rq_8f3a2c, rq_8f3a9d. Root time window: 2025-11-05T09:12Z -> spike at 09:18Z. Any idea why we'd get cross-region routing when eu was still 'up' in the console?

jess_support: sorry you're hitting that. can you paste one or two full response headers from a failing request? also are you using the region-specific hostname (api.eu.redwood.com) or the global endpoint with a region preference header?

acme_ops: we use the global endpoint (api.redwood.com) + header X-Redwood-Region: eu and also set "region_affinity":"strong" in our client. headers from a failing call: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: rq_8f3a9d
x-redwood-route: us-west1
x-redwood-quota-remaining: 0
date: Wed, 05 Nov 2025 09:18:32 GMT
```
Body was {"error":"quota_exhausted","message":"region capacity exceeded, falling back"} 

acme_ops: note: in console eu metrics showed 70% utilization not 100% at that time. so curious why it fell back.

miguel_sre_oncall: tagging in. quick note: console metrics are averaged over minute windows + include queued capacity. If you saw 70% avg but there were short bursts that temporarily exhausted concurrent slot limits, the router will consider per-availability-zone and per-pool headroom before routing. fallback can trigger if the local pool reports no free slots. Also cross-region fallbacks will show x-redwood-route with the region name — that's expected.

jess_support: two things we'll collect: 1) a short pcap or HAR of the calls around spike, 2) the exact client config for batching/streams. In the meantime, can you try forcing eu using the region host to see if behavior changes? i.e., curl https://api.eu.redwood.com/v1/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"prompt":"test"}'

acme_ops: tried that — when hitting the eu host directly we still saw some 429s but they were less frequent. full headers show x-redwood-pool: eu-c-prod-12 and x-redwood-slot-availability: 0 for failing requests.

miguel_sre_oncall: that header is useful. suggests pool-level exhaustion (dedicated vs shared pools differ). couple of clarifications: are you on Reserved/Dedicated capacity or on Shared (hosted) tier?

acme_ops: hosted tier. we have burst enabled but not dedicated.

elena_product: fyi from product: current global failover policy is ordinal: prefer region -> if pool reports slot_unavailable -> attempt other regions in reorder [eu, us-west, us-east, asia]. There is a short soft-retry path (100-200ms) before falling back; if retries fail we route to fallback region. That short retry can create a tail latency bump. If you want strict regional pinning, use the region-specific host or request a dedicated region reservation.

acme_ops: is there any way to avoid cross-region 429s triggering from our side? like client retries or a header? our client is sensitive to latency so failover to us-west kills UX.

jess_support: options: 
- set region pinning (api.eu.redwood.com) — avoids routing hops but you'll be limited to eu pool capacity
- request a quota top-up / burst increase for eu (we can file an internal support request)
- enable "graceful-degradation" where short prompt truncation or token limit reduction is applied before retrying to fallback region (our SDK supports a reduce_tokens_on_throttle_flag)

miguel_sre_oncall: also check that you're not hitting per-account concurrent request limits. We enforce both pool-level slots and per-account inflight caps. If your client opens many connections in parallel, the router may deny at the account layer even if pool overall looks fine. Example check: in logs search for lines like `account_inflight_exceeded account=acct_123 inflight=120 limit=100`.

acme_ops: ahh we do have bursts from our frontend — looks like in the spike we had 180 concurrent prompts originating in a 2s window. limit might be 100. how best to smooth?

elena_product: smoothing tips: use client-side soft-queueing (throttle to X concurrency), or enable our batching option — it can combine small prompts into single token batches reducing slot pressure. We also have SDK config `max_concurrency` and `batch_window_ms`.

acme_ops: can you share a quick repro script so we can reproduce locally and show you logs?

jess_support: yes — try this k6/hey-style script to simulate a spike. replace $KEY: 
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total} %{header_x_request_id}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
    -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu" \
    -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' \
    https://api.redwood.com/v1/completions &
done
wait
```
That fires 200 concurrent requests. If you reproduce 429s with x-redwood-route != eu then we confirmed router fallback under pressure.

acme_ops: running now... confirmed: 429s start around iteration ~120 and many of those show x-redwood-route: us-west1. sending results to you.

miguel_sre_oncall: thanks — can you also include the `x-redwood-pool` and `x-redwood-slot-availability` headers from failing responses? we want the pool-ID.

acme_ops: attached in thread. failing responses show `x-redwood-pool: eu-c-prod-12` and `x-redwood-slot-availability: 0` for most 429s. some 429s had `x-redwood-pool: eu-c-prod-13` with slot-availability: 2 but `x-redwood-account-reqs: 110/100` (i.e., account inflight cap exceeded).

jess_support: ok that's actionable: two root causes colliding — pool-level intermittent exhaustion during microbursts, plus per-account inflight limit tripping. We'll open an internal ops ticket to review pool autoscaling thresholds and per-account caps for your account. I'll request a temporary bump while you smooth traffic.

elena_product: long-term we recommend either dedicated reservation for eu or SDK-level client throttling + batching. We can also evaluate adding a soft-prefetch buffer in your client so tail requests wait 150ms and then either batch or drop gracefully.

acme_ops: appreciate it. one more Q — when fallback happens and client gets routed to us-west, billing shows consumption in us-west too right? we need those metrics for cost center tracking.

jess_support: yes — billing and usage are attributed to the region that actually served the request. So cross-region fallback will appear as us-west usage. We'll include that in the escalation note so finance can expect swapped metrics during the spike.

miguel_sre_oncall: next steps I'm taking: 1) open ops ticket to review eu-c-prod-12 scaling logs around 09:18Z 2) temporarily raise account inflight cap for acct_... to 200 while you deploy client throttling 3) monitor for 1 hour and report back.

jess_support: I'm filing the support escalation now, will attach your HAR + sample logs. ETA for ops ack: ~15-30m.

acme_ops: thanks all. we'll implement client-side max_concurrency=80 and batch_window_ms=20 and rerun the spike test, will post results shortly. :thumbsup:

route-bot: Incident 2025-11-05-INTL-429 created by miguel_sre_oncall. Priority: P2. Linked: support-1923459999.

acme_ops: update — with client concurrency capped at 80 and batching enabled, rerun shows almost zero cross-region fallbacks, latency tail improved from 1200ms -> 240ms median. very happy with results. will keep monitoring and await ops confirmation on the pool scaling.

jess_support: great — closing loop once ops posts final notes. leaving ticket open until pool scaling review complete. :white_check_mark:"
